Q: Exporting an array in bash script A:

I saw a lot of unclear ideas and a lot of text. But I couldn't find an elegant solution.
(Perhaps due to the many replies my post will not be seen.)
1. Environment variables are only visible to child scripts (which are launched from the current script). But child scripts cannot affect parent environment variables in any way.
2. In order for independent scripts to exchange data, a clipboard file is needed.
3. the best import is through the declare and source directives

To write an array to an environment variable
use

export MY_ARR="$(declare -p my_arr)"

Attention: line breaks are not saved in environment variables. Additional shielding is required.

Example (not been tested)

export MY_ARR="$(echo -e "$(declare -p my_arr)"|sed ':a;N;$!ba;s/\n/\\\\n/g')"

To import it into the script


 source <(echo -e "${MY_ARR}")

To exchange variables between scripts
(Code as an example. May need some modification)

UPDATE:(In the previous edition there was a solution through descriptors. But this solution complicates the code due to the inability to control the descriptor pointer. In the new edition, the example is simplified and a specific file is specified as the clipboard)

./sare_space.sh

#!/bin/bash
script_share_space_path=$(dirname $(readlink -f "$0"))
_byffer_path="$script_share_space_path/buffer"
touch "$_byffer_path"

exportVar(){
    echo "$@"
    declare -p "$@" >"$_byffer_path"
}

importVar(){    
    source <(cat "$_byffer_path"|sed 's/^declare -- //')  
}

./my_lib.sh

source "./sare_space.sh"
otherLib(){
    exportVar "var_1" "var_2"
    "./otherLib.sh" $@ 
    importVar
}
otherLib

./otherLib.sh

source "./sare_space.sh"
importVar
#... code
exportVar "var_1"

The idea is simple:
1 Before calling a child script, you must export the variables for that script and import the variables passed by the child script.
2. In a child script, you need to import the variables of the parent script before executing. After the child script completes, export the child script variables.
3. Previous buffer data will be erased with each export(write) attempt. Therefore, you must always follow the previous 2 rules, and then there will be no problems with nesting or sequence of calls.

4.The idea comes down to calling scripts sequentially. For parallel execution of scripts (when 2 scripts are launched in parallel), the idea needs to be implemented via "mkfifo"

All rules boil down to the following:
what is transmitted to the recipient must be read at the earliest opportunity. Otherwise there will be uncertainty

Q: Object doesn't collide A:

If you want to use the isTrigger you need to check the collision with OnTriggerEnter. If you want to use the OnCollisionEntertry adding a rigidBody to the cube with the is kinematic (for performance) flag, disable the is trigger from the sphere and see if that works.

Check the difference of the methods here:

https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Collider.OnCollisionEnter.html https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Collider.OnTriggerEnter.html

Regards
